I often feel like there is just no point in getting up anymore, and I've been having thoughts that everyone would be better off if I just disappeared.\n\nDoctor: Have you had any changes in your sleep lately, such as trouble falling asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual?\n\nPatient: I haven't really noticed any specific changes in my sleep patterns, like having trouble falling asleep or waking up too early. I just find myself staying in bed a lot of the time because I feel so completely exhausted and have absolutely no motivation to get up.\n\nDoctor: Have you noticed any change in your appetite or weight over these past seven months, such as eating much less or much more than usual?\n\nPatient: Yes, food has completely lost its taste to me, and I have no desire to eat anymore. I usually have to force down just a few bites of toast or soup so my sister doesn't worry, and I often skip meals entirely. Because of that, I've lost weight and my clothes are hanging much looser on me now.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had any other periods like this before that lasted at least two weeks, even if they were not as severe?\n\nPatient: No, I have never experienced a period of depression or sadness like this before. This is the very first time I have ever felt this way, and it all started only after my mother passed away.\n\nDoctor: Since your mother passed away, have you been able to have any moments of comfort or enjoyment when you think about her, or has the sadness and emptiness stayed constant and overwhelming most of the time?\n\nPatient: No, I haven't found any comfort at all, and the sadness and emptiness have been completely constant and overwhelming for these past seven months. It feels like a heavy gray cloud is always sitting on my chest, and all the joy has been completely drained out of my life.\n\nDoctor: Did these symptoms start only after your mother passed away, and have they stayed constant and severe most days for the entire seven months without easing up?\n\nPatient: Yes, all of this—the deep sadness, losing interest in everything, the thoughts about God punishing me, and hearing my mom's voice—only started after she passed away. It has been completely constant and heavy every single day for the last seven months, without a single day of relief.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms begin within a month of your mother’s death, and have they felt out of proportion to what you expected after the loss?\n\nPatient: No, they didn't start right away, as I kept busy organizing her funeral and community events at first, but this severe sadness and loss of interest really took hold about three months later when the seasons changed. It definitely feels far worse and more paralyzing than normal grief, completely draining the joy out of everything and making me feel like there's no point in even getting up.\n\nDoctor: Did these symptoms start within a month of your mother’s death, or did they begin later and only after you had been grieving for some time?\n\nPatient: They didn't start right away within the first month, as I kept busy organizing her funeral and community events at first. It was only about three months later, when the seasons changed and we had to face our usual traditions without her, that this heavy sadness and numbness really set in. So it has been about seven months now that I've been feeling this way.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms begin within one month of your mother’s death, or did they start later after you had already been grieving for some time?\n\nPatient: They started later, about three months after she passed away. At first, I was keeping myself busy organizing her funeral luncheon and church events, but the deep sadness and emptiness really set in about seven months ago.\n\nDoctor: Have you been hearing your mother’s voice or believing that God is punishing you even when you know these experiences may not be real? This helps me understand whether there are psychotic symptoms along with the depression.\n\nPatient: Yes, at night I hear my mother's voice scolding me, saying I ruined everything and am a burden. I also feel convinced her death was a punishment from God, seeing signs in off-time church bells and flickering streetlights. While others tell me it's just in my head, it feels so real to me, though it only started after I fell into this deep depression.\n\nDoctor: Do the voice you hear and the belief that God is punishing you happen only when your mood is very low, or have you ever had these experiences when you were otherwise feeling okay?\n\nPatient: No, I never experienced those things before my mood became so low. I never heard her voice or had those thoughts back when I was still feeling okay.\n\nDoctor: Before your mother passed away, or after your mood improved, did you ever have any similar symptoms, or have all of these symptoms stayed tied to this loss and then gradually improved over time?\n\nPatient: No, I never had any of these feelings, the voices, or the thoughts about God before my mother passed away. I didn't feel these severe symptoms within the first month because I threw myself into organizing her funeral and community events to stay busy. It was about seven months ago, roughly three months after she died, that the deep sadness and loss of interest really set in as the reality of her absence sank in.\n\nDoctor: Did your severe sadness and loss of interest begin within 1 month after your mother died, or did it start later after you had already been grieving for some time?\n\nPatient: No, it didn't start within that first month because I initially kept busy organizing her funeral luncheon and church events. It was only later, about seven months ago as the seasons changed and the traditions arrived without her, that the deep sadness and loss of interest truly took hold.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms start within one month of your mother’s death, or did they begin later after you had already been grieving for some time?\n\nPatient: They definitely started later, not within the first month. Right after my mother died ten months ago, I threw myself into organizing her funeral and church events to keep busy. The deep sadness and loss of interest really set in about seven months ago, once the holidays and familiar traditions arrived without her.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms start within one month of your mother’s death, or did they begin later after you had already been grieving for some time?\n\nPatient: They started later, about three months after she died. Immediately after her death ten months ago, I stayed busy organizing her funeral and community events. Back then, I was always very active with church socials and baking, and I never felt this way.\n\nDoctor: Have your symptoms been severe enough to make it hard to function at work, at home, or in your relationships most days?\n\nPatient: Yes, they have made it almost impossible to function. I've completely pulled back from church and neighborhood activities, and I've let my house and garden go untended. Some days I can't even get out of bed to cook or bathe, so my sister has to constantly check in to make sure I'm taking basic care of myself.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms start within 1 month after your mother’s death, or did they begin later after you had already been grieving for some time?\n\nPatient: They started later, about three months after she passed away. Immediately after her death ten months ago, I kept busy by organizing her funeral and community events. The severe depression and loss of interest didn't set in until about seven months ago, as the seasons changed and the reality of her absence really hit me.\n\nDoctor: Did your symptoms start within 1 month of your mother's death, or did they begin later after you had already been grieving for some time?\n\nPatient: They started later, about three months after she passed away. At first, I stayed busy organizing her funeral and community events to keep my mind occupied. It was only about seven months ago, as the seasons changed and we had to face our usual traditions without her, that the deep sadness and loss of interest really set in.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks before your mother died when you felt depressed or lost interest in things, even without a major loss or stressor?"
